text: Gateway Classic Cars in Lousiville should be ashamed of themselves. You would think that a company claiming to be the large dealer of classic automobiles would pride themselves on their products and customer service, not in my case however. I wanted to purchase a classic truck and using the internet came upon Gateway Classic Cars in Lousiville website. On their website they provide links to view automobiles that they sell and the site also provide a description of the automobiles. I selected the link to view for a 1965 Chevy c-10 pick up truck. In the video the truck looked to be in pristine condition. The engine was running, both head lights working, no cracked windows....However, after purchasing the truck, I discovered otherwise. What I actually received from Gateway Classic Cars in Lousiville was a truck that needed to be pushed off the lift and into my driveway. Because the engine did not start, I had to have it towed to a mechanic. After my mechanic looked over the truck, the following items were also discovered: the choke was broken, no speedometer cable, bad spark plugs, no horn, or working wiper switch, and the front brakes were worn down to almost nothing. Along with a broken driver side window and 1 head light not working... While it cost me $1300.00 to fix all the problems with the truck, I asked Dennis Severs, the sales manager for Gateway Classic Cars in Lousiville to reimburse me, for the engine problem, cracked headlight and broken side window. At first he Mr. Severs deny there was a problem and blame it on "bad gas." After speaking with Brad Kline the Sales Manager of all Gateway Classic Cars showrooms, I was provided with no resolution. Instead their offer was $250.00 and I have to sign what they called their "standard release" which would prohibit me from writing this. First, let me say in my opinion, the pictures and video shown on Gateway Classic Cars website of the truck I purchased, did not provide a good resemblance of the truck that Gateway Classic Cars actually delivered to me. In my opinion, after viewing the truck up close, the paint was an average at best, (while the pictures on the website looked great). I will never purchase from them again. But if you are thinking about buying from them be very careful...

text: I joined Franco's on Magazine in February (2015) and really enjoy it. It is always very clean, the staff is very friendly and helpful, and lots of machines to work on. The only con of many many pros is that is can be a little loud sometimes, especially when multiple classes are going on. The price is fairly reasonable ($89/mo), but includes most of the classes. I also have to recognize my personal trainer, Luke White. I started out very out of shape, with asthma, and just off of physical therapy for an injured shoulder. Luke has been very careful to not push too hard, but still make significant progress. He is always prepared ahead of time with the exercises he is going to have me do, and I can tell he has put careful thought into each session. Luke maximizes each session by engaging multiple muscle groups and combines body weight exercises and more focused machine exercises. He also is great at explaining what is behind each movement, the importance of proper breathing and cool down, and we talk about nutrition. And the best part, I've lost almost 15 pounds in a little over 2 months!

text: We found this place while out cycling and taking a tour of historical places celebrating Dr Martin Luther King. I must admit, that we were totally prepared for (and okay with) it being a dive. Probably the quickest split check situation is ever encountered! Food more tan exceeded my expectations! I split the Lizzardi Rolls with a fellow rider. They were fresh, fried to perfection, and served with a sauce that was equal parts sweet, tangy, and spicy! For an entree, I had the stuffed baked bell pepper - stuffed with shrimp, crab and ground beef. The entree came with a choice of two sides. I opted for red beans and rice and steamed broccoli. Everything was cooked just perfectly! Two in our party ordered fried catfish plates. I was lucky enough to snag a bite and, I have to say, that's what I will be getting next time! text: After spending forever looking for a room I finally found this place and it seemed decent so I booked it. Then I read the Yelp reviews and got nervous. Too many Yelpers have had run in with the manager and I find that (still) worrisome. However, my stay was uneventful in the best way possible and the price was great! Check in and check out were super easy and the staff was welcoming. The room had exposed brick wall, high ceilings, a ceiling fan, large, bright window into the courtyard, tv, microwave, free wifi that worked just fine, and a bathroom with new fixtures. The room was clean and cozy with a large and super comfy bed. My own gripe was that the only place in which I could plug in my phone was at the microwave where there was a power strip. There is a breakfast buffet in the courtyard which I suppose in cold weather wouldn't be much fun but given the layout, I don't see where else they would put it. Regardless, I was happy for some breakfast and hot coffee. I cannot complain about the noise. When I was in the bathroom I could easily hear my neighbors but once I went into the sleeping area I couldn't hear anyone. The building is old so of course it creeks and you can hear people walking around above your head. Big deal! You want to the Ritz, go stay there but I was happy in this historic building. I liked that I could walk right out of my room and find a bench and table in a quiet area in which to relax. The hotel is right near Walgreens and the trolly and it is in a nice, quiet area. I loved walking around the French Quarter all day and I was just as happy to come home to a quiet, cozy spot the sleep. I'm tempted to stay here again.

text: Yelp Fit Club had an event at the Barre Body Studio today, which was a great opportunity to check out the facilities. I have taken a couple of barre classes before in other cities but by no means am I a pro. First off, Barre Body Studio is the most upscale and luxurious barre studio I've been in. It's clean, elegant and modern for such a small space. Registration and check in was easy. There are free lockers with keys for your stuff. The bathrooms (with showers) were clean and had lots of amenities. There was a water cooler in the back too that does both hot and cold drinks. There were even chandeliers hanging in the Barre rooms!! There's also a glow juicery in the lobby for a healthy post workout drink. The only thing I'd change (and this is probably due to lack of space) is that the bathrooms weren't really in a separate private area; it was more of an extension of the main studio. The locker area got quite crowded too before and after class. Megan was out fearless leader for the hour, and she worked us hard! I got a well-rounded workout, from arms, to abs, to legs, to butt (and a smattering of cardio too). The hour just flew by! I will say that the room was a bit crowded though with over 20 people. Sorry to my neighbours that I inadvertently hit! Hopefully their regular classes aren't as full. There were a couple times that I found it hard to see the instructor because of everyone there. Megan was great at accommodating all levels with modifications, and helped one on one with technique too. Compared to the other barre classes I've taken, this class had less emphasis on the barre, and more on weights, ball, floor, resistance band exercises. It was a bit less cardio than I've experienced in other classes too. She did mention that every class is different though. I personally like more time at the barre, because this is what makes the workout unique! Barre Body Studio has a $40 for 2 weeks trial offer, as well as monthly, 5 and 10 class pass and drop in rates. I had a great experience here and would definitely come back for another class!!

text: Jenna is AMAZING. I found Hair Passion through Wedding Wire while looking for a hair stylist for my May 9th 2015 wedding. She was top rated there and on Yelp, and her website and example photos looked great. I contacted her about prices, and she is incredibly reasonable for the services she provides. She was willing to come to the church I was getting married at in Noblesville, IN to do my hair as well as my four bridesmaids updos. I went to her salon for a trial run two weeks before the wedding. We discussed styles for myself and my girls and did a run through that looked great. My hair is thinner and doesn't hold curl well so she gave me some tips for pre-wedding hair planning and maintenance. She is so warm, friendly and professional - we clicked instantly. I paid for half of the total (myself and the maids) in advance, and she would take the rest on the day of in cash or check. On my wedding day she was early, and came fully prepared. She even brought me a wedding gift! A card, Mr. & Mrs. shaving cream set, bobby pins, and hairspray. So sweet. She stayed for 5 hours with us and we had so much fun. My hair was GORGEOUS! I kept my hair down and in dramatic curls, with one side partially pinned back. My floral crown was too big for the art deco style we wanted to go with, so she helped me take it apart and we pinned fresh flowers in my hair, as well as made impromptu hair pieces for all of my girls. She was calm and totally ok with improvising at the last second with me. We used a partial netted veil pinned in with the flowers. We also added a long veil to the back of my hair for the ceremony. I took the long veil out at the reception and just kept the flowers and the netting. My hair style lasted ALL DAY AND NIGHT. That never happens for me! It was windy during pictures and it stayed in place, it got humid after it rained (and my wedding reception was in a garden pavilion so I was inside and outside a lot), and it stayed after I danced my ass off all night with my guests. My bridesmaids each selected an undo they wanted (each was different) and Jenna pulled them all off flawlessly. She made floral hair pieces for each and spent extra time making everything perfect. I got so many compliments on my hair at my wedding. I will never be able to thank Jenna enough for helping to make my wedding day so perfect.

text: I had a furnace diagnosis done. $250. PROS: neat, clean, polite, on time CONS: expensive, pricing unclear, slow, charged labour rates to order parts and check on warranty, felt very sketchy. I hired this company based on reviews from homestars site but later discovered the site is not considered to be very reputable. I thought the cost was $109 for the diagnosis but that is the cost to show up. Then they charge $129 per hour labour. I wouldn't have hired then if I understood that. However, even though they were unclear, I thought the misunderstanding was reasonable (though disappointing). The tech took the entire hour to "diagnose" the problem with 20 minutes of that hour spent in his vehicle.....checking on the warranty coverage. I don't think that this is legitimate part of the labour fee. Certainly the company I eventually hired didn't charge me labour for those things. The second thing about the length of the diagnosis (exactly one hour), is that I knew what the problem was, I knew the error codes and told the tech. I needed the Hvac certified diagnosis to get the warranty. It's very simple issue to diagnose....I could appreciate that there are some standard best practices and extras to check to see if there maybe additional problems but it really shouldn't have taken more than 30 minutes at the absolute most (with all the extras)! The third thing I was disappointed about was I told the company before coming was that it was a warranty job and I wanted the job under warranty. I was VERY CLEAR about this. I mentioned it twice on the phone and once by email. They told me after they had completed the diagnosis and I had paid the bill that they would offset my bill by the warranty amount but wouldn't do the job for the amount provided under the warranty (100% parts and labour). To be fair, I dealt with three other companies and the warranty amount provided is less than market rates in Edmonton. One company even denied there was a warranty. It is not popular. The warranty company warned me about this and I warned First Call. If they had been up front and honest that they would charge me extra, I would not have hired them and I felt taken advantage of. It seemed dishonest to me to say you will accept warranty work but then charge the client extra. Fourth, I was rather aghast when the tech told me I should appreciate their willingness to offset the warranty because some companies will submit warranty claims without telling the homeowners and pocket it as profit.......whaaaaaaaattttt? I'm giving this place two stars rather than one because I think they may have been poorly represented by this employee. Their pricing is still higher than average but they are readily available. So if you need something done quickly, they can likely accommodate you without having to pay their overtime rate. I would suggest that you stay with them while working to insure you are charged for genuine labour. I would also make sure you agree up front that "truck time" is not "labour".

My sister ordered the $9.50 blackened cajun chicken poboy (fully dressed) and I the ~$7 ham & eggs poboy. Hers was absolutely great; mine was plainly just ham. And eggs. Eh, although a bit my fault. We luckily arrived before the lunch rush, and our total time in and out (we ordered to-go) was about 25 minutes. I had to make a second trip, so I went back a few days later to satisfy my muffaletta craving. Good lord. It's possibly the biggest sandwich I've ever had. I'm not ashamed to say I finished the entire thing either. Well-rounded olive salad, plenty of salami, and I have absolutely no regrets for ~$10. However. The crowd at 12:30 pm was out the door, and waiting in line took about 30 min alone. Was it a sigh-worthy wait? Yes. Was it worth it? I'd probably say yes as well. Overall, a solid poboy shop if you're looking for a bite in the French Quarter. Don't be in a rush and be fine with shabby/no seating, and you'll be quite satisfied. To suggest that Seafood Delight was either delightful or contained seafood would be an insult to my intelligence and eyesight. This dish should properly be called Broccoli Delight because that's the dominant ingredient, followed by fake crab and sundry other vegetables. There was an outrageous claim that the dish contained lobster. Well, if it did, my magnifying glass failed to detect any. Maybe, the person responsible for this travesty passed a piece of dessicated lobster over the dish, and by an act of "nearness" ascribes lobster to this miserable dish's components. As for the Mongolian Beef, it was surely the toughest and driest meat that I've ever attempted to eat. One saving grace is that I'm convinced that the chef was secretly attempting to introduce me to an exotic gourmet adventure by substituting Yak meat for the beef. This is a gruesome gift I could well do without. Overall, what is most appalling is the establishment's contemptuous treatment of its takeout customers. Places like this harbor a conceit that we don't know the difference between meat or seafood and vegetables, and that somehow we'll live with what we get because we're not present to complain or to send the food back as we might at a dine-in restaurant. text: I played Lederach on June 6, 2015 as part of a golf outing with a 2pm shotgun start. In addition, I have played a normal round at this course 2 or 3 times previous to this last round. What has kept me from writing a review before this past round is that I could not decide on a rating. If I am being completely honest, I have loved the course at times and I have also hated this course but at the end of the day it one of the nicer courses in SE PA. I can agree with at least some parts of all of the previous reviews that have been written here on yelp. I think that what everyone needs to keep in mind is that this is NOT a beginners golf course, it is long, the greens are tough (#1 and #8 are almost comical depending on pin placement), and it becomes an even tougher course if it is a windy day. This course is designed for a better than average golfer that has a good knowledge of how far they hit each of their clubs. Cons - The greens fees can be a little expensive but the course has always been well maintained when I have played there. Parts of the course do wind through a housing development but the houses only come into play on hole 18. Otherwise, you should probably look for an easier course if you are routinely finding yourself in a backyard. The rounds here can be slow but I think that is partially due to the difficulty of the course. I am all for different levels of players getting out to play so I just know ahead of time that rounds here will probably be 5 hours. Pros - It is a beautiful course with some really challenging holes. 9 and 18 are a great way to finish each 9. Each of the par 5's are a test of your golfing skills. This course has always been in great shape when I have played. I do not know of another course in the area that is similar to the layout at lederach. This is a course that needs to either be played a few times or played with someone that has been here before because the danger on most holes is not visible in the form of bunkers, creeks, or lakes. The dangers are being in the wrong part of the fairway where you have no angle to the green, hitting a false front, or being on the wrong tier of the green. Overall, I appreciate the design of the course and have respect for it as I know that it will always challenge my golf game. I will continue to visit but it will never be my favorite course due to the cost and distance from my house. It is great for a once a year round with my buddies.

text: Food: ***** Service: * I own a restaurant so I am overly sympathetic and empathetic when I am not getting top notch service- maybe it was a slammed lunch and our server is worn out, whatever. But when the offenses start piling up my empathy dries up. That's what happened with my highly anticipated, partially disappointing visit to Cold Springs Tavern. As an out of towner with a love of barbecue I was on a mission to try California-style barbecue. I had only read about CA's tri-tip beef contribution to the food genre and I was stoked to learn about the secluded Cold Springs Tavern from a local gal pouring wine in a tasting room in Los Olivos. So my wife and I made plans to eat a late lunch there the following day (yesterday, a Saturday). We found it, parked and were seated in the back room at about 2:20, the last turn before the 3pm close of lunch service. The room was quiet and tucked back but full of a group at a six top and two other couples at the only other two tops. The room was right next to the server stand and the kitchen entrance. A young lady took our drink orders (water and wine for my wife, a beer for me) after cleaning the floor of some dipping sauce that she spilled on the floor. She brought my wife's wine and left, returning to bring something to the table where she had spilled the sauce. That couple asked her to clean the sauce that was still on their table cloth and dripping down the side. She probably didn't see it, no sweat. A guy server took our food order after answering our questions and steering us toward what we wanted- awesome. Our cup of wild game chili came out. But my beer was nowhere to be seen- nor the water. After a couple minutes and went out to find her and see what was up. She said they're out of it. Okay, would have been nice to know that. She offered an alternative but I could get it at home so I walked to the bar to see my options- the bartender mentioned another CA beer that I didn't remember from the menu that I wanted so I got it and went back to my seat. The chili was amazing. A different guy server brought our sandwiches- the tri-tip in sauce and the tri tip option with sauce on the side as well as apple horseradish and salsa. They were awesome. I preferred the undressed option with sauces on the side. I ended up not using much sauce and much preferred the salsa with some of the horseradish. My side of potato salad was not with mine- forgotten by the kitchen or our server or both. Good- I wanted to change to the regular chili. Our girl server had been in the server stand area texting on her phone but she was not in sight- I saw the bartender and asked her, so she brought the chili. It was also very good. My wife needed another glass of wine- and the water, it was a hot day. Eventually my wife got up and tracked down our drink server and asked for another glass of wine and the water. Things are starting to turn sour at this point. The girl brings the wine and water, sets it down and walks off, no "Here you go!" or "How is everything?" We wrap up, ask one of the guys at the server stand if we can get a to go box and our check. The room is empty at this point. It's quiet, no music, an unwelcome feeling from the drink server, and we are now talking not about how good the food is but how jacked up our service has been. The fella who took our food order brings the box and the check, asks how everything was. We said food was awesome but our girl server "needs some work". He said the servers don't have sections and everyone kind of works all tables. While we're boxing up the leftovers our drink server comes into the room to go through a closed door in the corner behind my wife's chair. She kicks the leg of my wife's chair and again doesn't say a thing. We are definitely getting bad energy from her now. I leave a ~10% tip on the credit card slip and take it to the bar so I can explain the low tip. The bartender is not around and our salty drink girl is behind the bar so I leave the slip on the bar and we leave. I'm writing all this for two reasons. First, to defend my low tip. My wife and I run two food service businesses, a lunch spot and a dinner restaurant. The servers were undoubtedly talking about us and the low tip when we left and this is my only way of explaining to them what went down. I am a 20%+ tipper- unless the train really goes off the tracks, which it did. Second, hopefully management reads Yelp reviews. I sure do. Maybe the no section thing usually works but for us it didn't. If our girl servers function is drinks, then she needs some training. She smiled- initially- but her communication was non-existent (except for whoever she was texting with). It was a downer of an experience and it colored my mood for the next few hours.

text: To reiterate Sari A's post, what could I possibly say about Village Whiskey that you have read about in the past 1000 reviews. I can only provide you with my experience. The place is small. When I arrived with two of my friends, there were two seats available at the bar together, and another seat open separated by an individual who graciously moved down for my party. We managed to grab his seat upon his departure, for another friend. We were lucky that we got there when we did as the place became full of patrons waiting to get a seat. What this place lacks in size it makes up in every other aspect including the service and spirits at the bar, and the grub coming out of the kitchen. The bartenders were not there to just pour drinks. Whether it was the warm-up beers we ordered, to the glasses of whisky later, they provided a brief explanation of everything my compadres and I were considering. The bar is small, but I guess the upside of that is that the bartenders are more attentive. I never had to wait for drink. My bartenders were there to wait on me the minute I took my last sip. I can't remember their names, but they were two bartenders that worked last Friday (4/24/15) between 5-8pm. In regards to the grub coming out of the kitchen, let me start with the shrimp. The popcorn shrimp was crispy and seasoned a little more than the usual popcorn shrimp appetizers. After two glasses of Whisky, I broke down and ordered the Whisky King. I never imaged myself eating a burger with Foie gras on it, but I did, and I would probably do it again. In addition, the Applewood bacon, blue cheese, and the maple bourbon glazed cipollini onions, only enhanced the creation of flavors taking place between the buns. Despite the fancy presentation, the burger did not lose its simplicity, which is the flavor of the meat. There was only one way to close the show after this burger. That is right, an another glass of whiskey. Make it a 12 year please. An abundance of aged libations, creative burgers, and professional staff are the attributes that make Village Whiskey.

text: A touristy town like Santa Barbara needs its fair share of solid brunch spots. Cajun Kitchen is the Las Vegas act of brunch spots. It's consistent. It's working at multiple venues. It has its schtick (Southern-Creole cuisine), and it plays it well. It's sure to please without breaking the bank, but you can tell it's sung this tune many times before. And there's nothing wrong with that, CK is a well run restaurant. There's always a line on weekends, but it moves fast. Service is quick and attentive, with plenty of coffee on stand-by and salsa available if you ask for it. A word on the portions. Yes, they are fairly big, but they aren't colossal in the way some reviewers are saying. It's brunch. It's supposed to serve as two meals, and i you view CK's serving sizes through that lens you'll come out happy and satisfied. If there's too much you can save it for later. Just don't think this is Thanksgiving dinner, it's only bruch for god sakes. There omelets and scrambles are great. So are their po' boys, if you're feeling more like lunch than breakfast. Basically, if it has seafood and andouille sausage in it you can't go wrong. This time I tried the shrimp and grits (which includes a fair bit of andouille for good measure). While the sausage and seafood were great, the grits mixture was a bit oily. I had to cut it with some salsa- would have been better with toast, but maybe I neglected to order some. In any case, with Cajun Kitchen, you know what you're going to get: Solid. Themed. Brunch.

The mussels, which come in either a red or white sauce, are also a popular appetizer that my fellow diners raved about (I didn't try them since I ate about half the zucchini myself). As for entrees, the eggplant parm is actually better than similar dishes that I have tried at higher-end Italian restaurants, and the four cheese ravioli, which is served with a pesto alfredo sauce, is decadent yet delicious. And don't even get me started on dessert - I could eat their chocolate zuccotto cake for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The portions are extremely reasonable, so you definitely get your money's worth. The "family style" option is something to consider if dining with four or more people, since you get to choose multiple appetizers, pastas, meats, and desserts, all of which are all-you-can-eat. The service could not have been better. Our waiter was friendly, attentive, and - most importantly - extremely patient with our party of eight, who took what felt like decades to order.

text: Zahav is one of the most well-received restaurants in all of Philadelphia, and for very good reason. My dinner there was one of the best I have ever had, so let me break it down for you. After some debate, my party of four opted for the Tayim option, wherein you get the Salatim salad plates and your choice of hummus to share, plus two mezzes (small plates), one Al Ha'esh (entree), and one dessert per person. At $42 a head it may seem expensive, but as soon as the food starts coming, you'll soon realize it was worth it. The Salatim consisted of six small plates: beets, cabbage, beans, eggplant, grape leaves, and carrots. All were packed with flavor profiles that belied their simplicity. I point out the eggplant and beets in particular as the highlights among this bunch. The hummus came out at around the same time, and we chose the Turkish style. This hummus plate changed how I will think of hummus forever. Never have I eaten hummus served warm before, and now to eat it cold is unthinkable to me. Just get it and thank me later. At this point in the meal, my friends and I were already fairly satiated, but the best was yet to come. The mezze plates came out two or three at a time, which was a perfect cadence for us to fawn over each dish. The Tayim dining option is most advantageous due to the selection of mezzes, which between the four of us meant we could try 8/13 possible mezzes. All of our choices came out flawless, in taste and composition. If I had to rank them, it would be: Tier 1: Fried Cauliflower, Crispy Haloumi, House Smoked Sable Tier 2: Chicken Freekah, Grilled Duck Hearts, Yemenite Beef Stew Tier 3: Kibbe Naya, Crispy Lamb's Tongue Let me try to describe the Crispy Haloumi for a second. The layers of flavor as you chew the haloumi over and over in your mouth slowly uncover, and your eyes grow ever so slightly larger with each bite. That is the experience of eating this dish. I could probably write a paragraph about each of the mezzes, but on to the entrees. My lamb merguez was very good, but I think my palate had taken a beating from the round of mezzes. However, I also sampled my friends' branzino and sirloin, both of which were sparkling. The sirloin in particular was juicy though cooked rare, a pleasant surprise as I usually prefer more cooked steak. To top it all off, dessert was the perfect way to end a night of indulgence. The pumpkin basboosa and coffee custard were both a delight. Zahav has received a lot of hype on this website and elsewhere, and I will say that every word is well deserved. With a well-balanced menu, wonderful service, and a generally welcoming atmosphere, there is no reason you should have reservations about making your next reservation Zahav. Book in advance!

Not a difficult or time consuming order but it took well over 40 minutes for our food to arrive. The 'Philly Cheese Steak' was not a true cheesesteak (and since we are in the town famous for cheesesteaks, it was odd) but it was a good sandwich served with very good French fries. The cheeseburger as also cooked perfectly and served hot as was the hangar steak (served rare as requested) with a loose, sunny side up egg. The food was well above most hotel restaurant fare and we all felt our dishes were very good. If the service was better - faster - and the dining chairs less shabby looking; the rating for 13 would be much higher. text: I did it! NV Transformations works if you stick to the plan and lean on the great social media family for tips. I went through the orientation and was sneaking out the front door afterwards because this is a no excuse plan. I thought that there was no way that I could do this with a full time job and two kids under four. Luckily I bumped into a friend who made me realize I could do it as long as I pushed myself out of my comfort zone. I am so grateful I did not walk out the door that day because I am 22.8 lbs lighter in only six weeks. The workouts are five stars. I enjoy how every day is a different work out. There were even new moves I had never seen on my last workout of the six weeks. I appreciated that the coaches would provide modifications if needed. I am also a big fan of Zumba Dan. Coach Dan radiates positivity and confidence. His outlook is refreshing when you are sticking to the plan. One of the down things is that his class on Monday nights is in the small room and there are no real speakers. I love to dance and it is hard to get into it when the sound is clashing with the other room and the lights are full blast. It could also be that I was spoiled because I love the fact that in the main room workouts have lights go down and music goes up. It feels like a night club and it is a great change to the normal stale gyms. I felt that my challenge must have been one of the largest because the classes were pretty big. I am looking forward to the new location because that might mean a bit more personal attention will be available on how to improve or push myself. Don't get me wrong, when I asked for help I received it. I also appreciated that Eric made an effort to learn everyone's name even if he had to ask multiple times. The down side of the large classes was that I didn't really have "a coach." People on the facebook pages would refer to "their coach." To my knowledge I wasn't assigned to someone so I thought that I might have been missing out. It also seemed that the coaches rotated through classes so we had someone different typically. I also feel like there is an opportunity for clearer information when it comes to the meal plan. Much of the information that is needed is spread across three pages in the workbook and sometimes contradicts itself. I did not realize until the second week that I was not suppose to dip into the bottom bracket of food. I was also a bit unclear if I was to follow the weight on the portion sizes in the book or the palm, fist, cupped hands portions recommendations. I think I are way too much food the first week which made for a slow start. I did get great support from Jessica when I knew I was struggling with my meals. Overall, I would say that if you have tried everything, nothing worked, then this is what you need to do. It made me accountable for my own actions and has started some great habits why eliminating the bad ones. I signed up for another round to say the least.

text: I can say by far, this is the best Thai I've had in New Orleans. The attention to detail suggested a much more upscale environment than the pricing would suggest. Menu prices are reasonable, but drinks get pricey, our dinner for 2 ran us around $65 which included 1 cocktail and 1 glass of wine. The dishes we ordered, including the appetizer were full of flavor with subtle nuances of spice. Portion size was substantial, and the wait-staff were attentive but not helicoptering. If you plan to dine after 7, my suggestion is to make a reservation, because it fills up quickly with neighborhood locals. Parking is a challenge, but if you are from here or visit here enough, you probably already expect that. Where I was unable to give La Thai that 5th star was the fact that it promotes itself as Cajun Thai. And yes, there's options on the menu that contain crawfish, and the seafood options are plentiful - it takes more than that in my opinion to make that leap to being a Cajun restaurant. Spice is inherent in Thai food, as it is in Cajun cuisine - if there was a melding of that heat, I would've been more impressed. This was still the best Thai I've had in years, and I wouldn't hesitate to return, and I would hesitate to suggest it to visitors coming into town. It's in a beautiful area of Uptown; the staff are friendly and accommodating, and the food was delicious. It's a recipe that works, why not partake?

text: Went there for lunch yesterday before the drive home to Chicago. The service was good, but one of the meals that was clearly ordered came from the kitchen as a wrong entree. OOPS! It was tasty, with a traditional base and fresh vegetables and I would recommend it but it was good, but not great. I ordered a traditional Italian calzone, which came plated on a large plate and took up most of it. The marinara that was served in a small dish plated next to the calzone was a little watery but tasty none the less. The calzone dough was flakey and very buttery and the ham was cut into small cubes instead of shaved as I prefer it and overall the blend of ingredients made for a filling meal. One of our diners ordered the mostaccoli which had fresh zucchini and was delicious. The restaurant serves great meals overall and being that I'm a Chicago boy I am very familiar with great Italian meals. I can share that I would recommend this place if your downtown while in St. Louis. Be sure you do your best to get a table near the edge of the restaurant. Don't sit near the door on a cold day or you'll think you're eating street-side in February. BRRRRRRR!!!

text: We came here during Stone Crab Claw season. It starts Oct 15. They are expensive, around $30.50/lb, but they are good. The claws have some nice, juicy, sweet meat. If you want some good, fresh Stone Crab, go there from Oct. 15 through May 15. During peak days, this place can get super busy. They have a party like atmosphere. It's a place to get drunk with your friends at the beach. The decorations are all party-themed and gaudy. Their ceviche comes in a huge cocktail glass. It was very garlicy and nice. I loved the strong flavor of raw garlic inside. Sure, it might not be too traditional, but hey I liked it. The seafood goodies inside was fresh too. I could've done without the potato chips and the corn though. Their chowders can be skipped. They're super thick and clumpy. They seem very sweet and too creamy. It's not smooth or done with any grace. I would avoid. Their original grouper sandwich is huge. It's not a dinky sandwich. It's pretty enormous. It comes with American cheese. I like their fried grouper. They fry it well and the flavor is good. The bun is cheap, supermarket bun. But hey it kinda works. Although for the price, I wished they used something other than cheap super-market type ingredients. Their Fish Tacos are gigantic too. They stuff the hell out of the tortillas. I don't know if you can actually hold it and eat it. You might need to eat it with a fork. They give you two tacos per order, but trust me, they're plenty. Each taco is mini Willy's burritos. Overall, I think they're overpriced. But they have strong drinks and decent food. They have a "fun" atmosphere and the servers are good. I liked it.

text: Not the best car buying experience. I was in the market for a 2015 Toyota Tundra 1794 edition. Mind you this is a $50K+ vehicle so not cheap. Called up multiple dealers, received some bad service from 2 of the initial contacts. Sales guy (Mike Villari) here said he would honor the Truecar estimate I had and gave his word on excellent service and seamless transaction. Great right? Wrong! So I go there with my boss (vehicle was company lease). Went over all the options and the spec sheet which the salesman said is exactly what we would get in the vehicle we were going to lease and went through the credit process and made a deposit. At one point, the salesman discreetly throws away the original spec sheet and has a new spec sheet with less options for the same price (the good old bait and switch). So then, my boss was pissed off and wanted to cancel the whole thing. This is when the sales manager (Steve Tagye) got involved and to make it up to us, he said he would honor the original spec PLUS add in an upgraded navigation system. So, we mulled about it and decided to do it despite the trickery we encountered. My boss also wanted a hardcover truck bed cover for the vehicle so Mike quoted us $1100 (although not written) and GUARANTEED us that it would be ready for installation come the 1K mile service. Fast forward a month, and we come in for the service and lo and behold the bed cover is not there. Mike visited me in the waiting room and told me that he'll knock off $100 for the cover and ENSURED me that it would be ready within a week. Couple days later, he texts me saying that not only would it take an additional 2-3 weeks, but the sales manager REQUIRED us to pay up front for it and then Mike said it was $1500! (BAIT AND SWITCH AGAIN!) WOW..Sufficed to say, I cancelled the order. I'm not sure if they even put in the order because the guy I am going to to purchase the bed cover said it can be done in a couple days (and much cheaper). All in all, when you go to this dealership, make sure you have your deal in writing as their word is not worth a damn thing. I probably will not do business with this dealership again. text: We ate here last night for our anniversary dinner and were so excited to try a new (to us) place! Long story short, we were underwhelmed. If you don't feel like reading the novel that is to come, here's the short: Food: 4/5 stars, Service -1/5 stars, ambiance, 3/5 When he made reservations he told them we were coming for our anniversary. Usually places do something for you to celebrate with you, like seat you at a more private or romantic table or at least a verbal mention. No acknowledgement. No big deal, we don't need a standing ovation, it's just that most places realize that you do it up big for a special event that you took the time to mention, and that they're lucky you chose them. The hostess was sweet and sat us right away, didn't ask to take our coats. We were seated by the window facing the street, which would have been nice except that these are usually doors that are open for open air seating. They were sealed closed with a clear tape, but there was a literal wind blowing the menu insert and my hair around. It's December, I'm in a cocktail dress. You put us next to a windy freezing door in an otherwise empty restaurant? After about 5 minutes no one had come over (there was only 1 other table in the place) so my boyfriend tracked down the hostess and asked her to move us. She did right away and the new table was great (and at a comfortable temperature), So now we're back on track! We wait for awhile and finally an older blonde woman comes over and stands awkwardly far away from our table and says, "get you a drink?" Once we realized she was speaking to us, we asked for a drink menu. "don't you have one?" well, no, or we wouldn't have asked you. She returned, dropped it off and left us to decide. When she came back, I ordered a glass of wine and she asked me to repeat myself twice. You have 5-6 wines on the menu, how is this so difficult? So after more confusion and repeating, she leaves to get our glasses of wine. She brings them and tells us the special. I'm going to assume she meant chicken cacciatore soup but what she said was chicken skatatory soup. We pass on that, and I ask to have the salmon dish, without salmon, but with a different protein (that is listed as the same price). You would have thought I asked her to solve a difficult math problem. She made a big deal of it and finally agreed to ask the kitchen. She walked 10 feet away and asked and the guy in the kitchen said, "yeah, no problem" and was not at all phased, did not seem upset. She comes back and tells us we're ok, then leaves us to our wine. A bus boy brings us some bread in a cloth covered basket and it looks delicious! I pick it up to try it and it is ice cold. So why the basket? To keep it cold? Super disappointed. Food comes in a timely manner and is delicious. If there was a critique at all it would be that the scallops were a touch overdone, but were still very enjoyable. Ok, starting to forget about the negative stuff, back to enjoying our anniversary! She comes and asks if we want dessert. I remember that on the dessert menu were also dessert drinks and I ask her for a dessert menu. She looks up at the ceiling and starts rattling off desserts. I tell her that I don't want dessert, but I do want a dessert drink, which was listed on the dessert menu. This is of course an enormous inconvenience. We get the menu and I order a boozy coffee with no whipped cream. Guess how she delivered it to me? Yep, a mountain of whipped cream. When I point out that I asked for none, she corrected me and told me that I asked FOR whipped cream. I assured her that I did not, and pointed out that the only reason I asked for NONE was because the menu lists that it comes with and I don't like whipped cream. So again, this is a huge ordeal as she huffs 6 feet over to the bar to have another one made. I'd like to point out that we were her ONLY table. The table that was there when we were seated was gone and another younger blonde waitress was tending to a table of 2, the only other table in the place. At no point was she even remotely friendly. At no point did she smile. This may have been the worst service I've ever had, and if not, it comes close. So, if you're looking for a special place to celebrate a special event, think twice about this place. We'd go back again if she wasn't there.

I had the Paneer Tikka Masala (with some plain naan for dipping, etc), and my wife had the Vegetable Biryani. They were both terrific (although I think we both liked mine best). Seasoning was perfect (gotta love it when you aren't even tempted to add salt or pepper) - we both got level "3" on the spicy scale and that was perfect, too. Good level of heat, but not enough to distract from the flavor. This place is really small (three 4-seater tables and three 2-seater ones, I think), and there was only one other patron in there - but our service was great, food came out hot and timely. We actually liked the atmosphere. I will definitely be back, and if I lived close enough, I'd certainly try their delivery service. Our 2 meals plus one side of plain naan and a garlic cheese naan appetizer (with only water to drink) was right at $30 before tax and tip. The food was definitely worth it, but maybe a tad too spendy for all the time eating for me. If you wanna do it on a budget, I'd say split a meal and double up on the inexpensive bread/appetizers. text: It is very rare that you get to write a review of an institution that has actually saved your life. At the age of thirteen I was diagnosed with a brain tumor and underwent brain surgery at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. The hospital has won many awards and accolades since its establishment, and I personally never received anything but the best of care while a patient. CHOP, as its more commonly known, admits more than 15,000 children each year; if the President's children were sick, they would probably be patients at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. If nothing else, I'm grateful my parents were able to get me the best medical attention possible. There is no doubt in my mind that a lesser hospital, employing less skilled surgeons, would have left me severely brain damaged, or worse. Once arriving at CHOP, my parents, grief-stricken upon learning of my diagnoses, immediately calmed down. The doctors and nurses had a great bedside manner, the perfect mixture of comfort and professionalism. I remember very little from the day of my surgery. An IV was stuck into my arm and an anesthesiologist sedated me. My neurosurgeon was Doctor Suttor, chief of the neurosurgery division at CHOP. I regained consciousness a few hours later, back in my hospital room. The surgery was a success. When I woke back up I wanted nothing more than a cool drink of water. The doctors forbid me from drinking liquids and I had to be content with ice chips. My head pounded and my hair had been shaved during the surgery. There were twenty staples in the back of my head and all of them itched like hell. After the surgery, I couldn't control the entire right side of my body. It was almost as if I had a stroke, except my right arm and leg shook constantly and uncontrollably. There were bed rails on either side of the hospital bed, as if I were a toddler who just graduated from his crib. It's not easy to get much sleep while you're in a hospital. As tired as I was, I couldn't get any rest. During those few times I was able to fall asleep naturally I would soon be woken up. A nurse would barge into my room, stick me with a needle, and shine a light in my eyes. In the days that followed I regained some control over the right side of my body. My limbs still shook constantly, but now I was able do things like hold a pencil or stand up while leaning against something for support. A physical therapist came by one day and I took my first steps outside the hospital room. My tumor was located in the cerebellum--the part of your brain that controls balance and motor skills, among other things. During such an invasive surgery there's bound to be some brain damage. It's no surprise that I was having trouble with walking and coordination. Immediately after the surgery, there was also concern I'd suffer from memory loss--the cerebellum also controls some cognitive functioning, like attention and memory. Fortunately, I was untouched mentally, but trapped inside a body my brain could no longer control. I was only able to walk on my own by using a gait belt to help with balance. Even then, I couldn't take more than ten steps at a time. A doctor came into the hospital room one day and handed me a plastic medical bag. Inside the hermetically sealed bag was the tumor they cut out of my head. My tumor was the size of a golf ball and pink like a wad of bubble gum. It felt empowering to hold in my hand what had once tried to kill me. I was able to hold down Italian water ice, but little else. I remember trying to eat an orange and vomiting all over myself after the first bite. I can't speak to the quality of hospital food, as even the smell turned my stomach. There was a bootlegger outside the hospital who sold VHS copies of movies still in their theatrical run, or not yet released on home video. My parents bought me a few tapes to play on the VCR in my hospital room. I think Titanic was the first movie I watched after the surgery. I could only handle watching television in fifteen-minute increments, so it took a long time before I finished the entire three-hour movie. There was a McDonald's in the basement of CHOP. I never understood why they let the world's unhealthiest fast food restaurant open up a location in a hospital; maybe they thought sick children wouldn't feel so bad if they were eating a happy meal. On my last day in the hospital I ordered a sausage and egg McMuffin with cheese. I ate the breakfast sandwich, a side of hash browns, and was able to keep everything down. It was a personal triumph. If I was able to handle the greasiest food in the world, there was a chance I wouldn't starve and waste away. All told, I spent a total of two weeks in the hospital. I was given the option of staying at CHOP and continuing my physical therapy there, but I opted to go back home and receive treatment at a local facility.

text: I rarely give 5 star reviews as few restaurants live up to their 5 star reputation however, I can guarantee you will love the experience at The Capital Grille. Classic surf and turf restaurant with strict attention to detail and impeccable service. The moment you step inside, the low mood lighting, quiet ambiance and classic decor instantly feels calming and inviting. We started Father's Day/Birthday celebration with the mother of all appetizers, The Grand Plateau, which consisted of lobster, jumbo lump crab meat, oysters, and colossal shrimp that sat atop a bed of ice and arrived on two tiers of UFO-like saucer trays. All I can say is WOW! Simply fresh and simply delicious. The nice touch was the lemon halves that accompanied the seafood. It was decoratively wrapped in fancy cheesecloth like material so as to catch the seeds when squeezing them. How clever! After tearing through the appetizers, the waiter brought us fresh hot hand towels scented with a squeeze of lemon. I felt like I was sitting in the First Class section on an airplane. Nice touch! The specials of the night were the Bone in- Filet Mignon ($62) which had a completely different taste than the regular menu Filet Mignon. It had a smokier, almost beef jerky-like flavor, but was a little drier than the regular Filet. The other special was the Lobster Bisque, a creamy and totally indulgent soup with large chunks of fresh lobster claw meat. Absolutely divine! I went with the regular menu Filet Mignon which was seasoned and cooked to perfection. We ordered several sides that were also great accompaniments to the meal: Sauteed Corn with Jalapeños, Mashed Potatoes, French Beans, and the ever popular Lobster Mac n Cheese. The sautéed corn was deliciously sweet and smoky with a bite from the jalapeños. Capital grille definitely doesn't skimp on the lobster in the lobster mac nor the lobster bisque. You get a good amount and won't feel robbed like other places. Prices are hefty for entrees but reasonable for sides, but quality and quantity eases the damage :) Overall, service was excellent and we never felt rushed, despite staying past the 10pm closing. I would definitely visit again.

text: If you are a golfer or not, this is a superb resort in the Tampa area. My wife enjoyed a relaxing day at the spa and bicycling around the resort. The dining rooms were beautifully appointed and the food was well prepared. Service was friendly yet professional. Innisbrook is certainly worth a visit and we look forward to returning.

text: Karl and Sarah Worley have taken their biscuits (and more) to a brick-and-mortar Biscuit Love restaurant in the Gulch (next to Bar Louie) with a line out the door! It opened last fall, but it took me that long to get up to Nashville (vs. rolling out of bed to the Farmer's Market down the street) to brave the lines to give the place a try. Like any Nashville hot spot, there's a line. We expected as much on Sunday morning, especially given it was CMA Fest weekend! We arrived around 10am I believe, and we were a little nervous about the number of people ahead of us. We were able to browse menus while we waited, as you stay in line as you move inside (and order at the counter) before receiving a number and being loosely directed towards available tables. I feel like we didn't have to wait long at all, because a lot of the groups were large and being a party of three we were ushered forward as tables opened up. The bar is first-come, first-served I believe, but be sure to ask a hostess/server checking on the line! Once we'd ordered, we were served quite quickly! Anna had a Bloody Mary and Dan had a craft beer. I needed caffeine so I had a delicious Arnold Palmer. Anna treated us to my favorite part of the meal... BONUTS. Fried biscuit dough (AMAZING) with sugar, lemon mascarpone, and blueberry compote. I seriously think that when I come back, I will make this my main meal, so I can have them all for myself. My. new. favorite. thing. I had a lot of trouble making up my mind for my main dish, because the menu at the restaurant is much more extensive than the truck's used to be. I decided that for my first visit, I needed to go with my old truck standby, the SEC: biscuit, smoked sausage, egg, and aged cheddar. I had the egg scrambled because I was in the midst of sensory overload when I ordered; I usually prefer the egg fried. But it was delicious nonetheless! Even better than the truck days, honestly... although I wonder if it's because I was eating it in air conditioning at a table with real silverware vs. plastic fork at the market. I also ordered sides of the "chronic" bacon which was sticky and sweet, and the potatoes. The potatoes I wish were a bit crispier, but the bacon was fab. Bacon purists might prefer the normal bacon, but I love a little sweetness with the salt. You guys, do yourself a favor and hit up Biscuit Love... I'm so glad I could take my friend Anna (and Dan, too!) to brunch there, and to meet Karl. I'm so happy for the Worleys and this new adventure, and hoping they put another location in Franklin someday!

text: Like most diners of Laurel, our reservation was made 2 months in advance for a weeknight dinner. Having almost all 5 star reviews, and rated as the #1 restaurant in Philadelphia, we were sure this was the safest bet for a memorable dinner out. Unfortunately, we were very disappointed with our experience. Read on to understand why. Our night started off fairly well, we were seated 15-20 min after our reservation. The restaurant is a small place so it was totally understandable. We brought an excellent napa cab to complement our dinner. After being seated our wine was opened and poured and bread and butter was served. This would have been great except that a table nearby with a cheaper wine was offered a decanter right off the bat without any request. We were not even offered the option which was a bit off putting. So note to servers, don't assume someone's wine should be decanted based on their appearance or age, ask if they would like it decanted. The rest of our service was fine, but that exchange rubbed us the wrong way. As for the food, I am shocked by all the amazing reviews. Did someone else make the food for our table? As we were eating almost everyone was making another reservation on their way out. W'ere we in the twilight zone? I wouldn't eat at Laurel again based on our experience. The arctic char and duck cossulet were both very good. If we would have had only those two dishes this restaurant would be a solid 4-5 star in my book. However, everything else we ordered was merely adequate to bad. At $16-34 per course, and overall $ 150-200 for a dinner out for 2 you expect amazing, and what was delivered outside of the two stand out dishes was shocking. Spending top dollar for great food is very rewarding, but nothing sucks more than paying a lot for a disappointing dinner. Biggest shocker of the night, the gnocchi was straight up gross. Slimy little pillows that disintegrate as soon as they enter your mouth. The texture combo was off putting. Slimy snot with pancetta bits is the best analogy. The fluke was fine. The fluke quality was great but the flavor was raw fluke and lime, nothing mind blowing there. The duck was adequate, but overpriced for the amount of duck you get... maybe 1/3 of a duck breast. The pork; gross. I could go on but you get the point. You can see what the chef is trying to do here with textural and flavor combos. However, for a dinner for two in which 8 dishes were ordered, you can't have only 2 good dishes, 1-2 passable dishes and the rest only edible because you know how much you paid for it. For restaurants of this level in Philly you expect so much more. Sbraga, Serpico, High Street, or Ela are far superior to Laurel if looking for a high end inventive meal. Nick Elmi seems like a nice guy, and coming out to say hi is a nice gesture, but kindness doesn't get me my hard earned money back. We really wanted to love this place but it was such a letdown.

text: First time for us, early on a buggy Friday evening. Overall, a decent stop for a quick BBQ fix. Friendly and casual, with some big, though unrefined flavors. Not sure why this is tagged "Peruvian". Collards, creamed spinach, mac n cheese, cornbread - more like Kansas City or East Texas to me. Service - friendly and quick. Prices - not bad for Q. Ambiance - non existent. Parking free and easy. We did a combo platter with chicken, pork, cornbread, fries and a slaw. We ordered the chipotle sliders and corn bread pudding ala carte. Chicken was really, really good. Crispy outside, super moist inside. Maybe a little over-brined but good overall flavor. We would get the chicken again. The pork shanks were nicely cooked. Really tender inside and a little crispy outside. I suspect they were braised in an oven, crisped on a flattop, and poured over with sweet/hot sauce. Pulled pork was uninspired; a little dry, not much fat, smoke or spice. I am not sure what they were going for. I mean, it was ok, but we'll try the sausage next time. Cornbread pudding was great, Slaw ok, cornbread side was a small, textureless loaf. Hand cut fries were there to catch the dripping sauce or rest your taste buds. A lot of folks comment on the great sauces, but we could not eat the chimichurri (dry herbs in vinegar, spicy with a chili-oil burn), the mayo or white bbq was a raw mouthful of garlic. The red bbq sauce seemed like commercial product with a little doctoring. We'll try it again sometime, and I will update. I would love to give Barbacoa another star or two because I applaud the concept and love the fact it is local, easy, fast, not too pricey and there is real BBQ void locally.

text: I have been to IOU several times, but finally decided I need to write a review in hopes that the owners of this business see it. We came in with a group of 4 for AYCE sushi at 8:10 pm and sat at the bar. There were 3 sushi chefs working and one server. It took at least 5 minutes for us to even be acknowledged and given drinks (just ice water). There were three tables being sat at, but all customers had finished their food. There were also two other couples sitting at the bar, one of which was just finishing up. So by no means was the restaurant busy. We let the chef know we were doing AYCE and ordered our first rolls. They took about 5-7 minutes to give us our first rolls. This continued to be the pace for the rest of our dining experience. After finishing one roll, we wait another 5 minutes (empty-plated) for the chefs to even acknowledge us, then another 5-10 to receive the roll. It should be mentioned that none of us ordered any deep-fried rolls (that take longer to prepare), so that cannot be an explanation as to why the service was so slow. At this pace, and with the menu's suggestion that dinner AYCE sushi should last 1 hour, it really did not feel like we were getting our money's worth ($25.99 for dinner AYCE). What's even worse-- at 8:47, the server started putting chairs on tables and asked us how we were doing our checks. To me, this is a not-so-subtle way of telling a customer they're finished. I found this extremely rude. As a server myself, it is both my restaurant's policy and my personal belief that chairs should not be stacked onto tables until all customers have left the restaurant, even if they are there past closing time. It's downright rude and creates a tense, unwelcoming atmosphere for your patrons. So all in all, we were given about 37 minutes of AYCE sushi at a painfully slow rate. I think I only ate 5 rolls; I could have gone for twice as much. And the real kicker is, the posted hours on IOU's door says that they closed at 10 pm. If I were a customer wanting to give them business and arriving past 9, I would be very irritated to drive to the restaurant only to find out that they closed a full hour before their posted hours. I suppose when you own your own restaurant you can do this at your discretion, but they're certainly losing business by doing so. I absolutely love IOU's sushi. The fish is always fresh-tasting with a good texture, the rice is a good consistency, and the rolls are unique and flavorful. But even amazing food cannot outweigh repeatedly terrible service. That's why it pains me to say that I won't be coming back to IOU.
label: NEG

text: How possibly could food this good come from a truck I ask you?! We stopped by the Franklin Farmers Market on Saturday morning. It's been a while since I've been to the farmers market in Franklin, I was surprised with how many booths and people were there. Anyway, we made our way to Crepe A Diem. They were easy to spot because of the red truck AND the long line. If a food truck has a line, you know it's good. We skimmed the menu and decided on getting a couple things and sharing them. We decided on the Louisiana crepe, which consists of Andouille sausage, provolone cheese, caramelized onions, and red pepper - Rouille sauce ($8.50). We ordered the garden sausage sandwich, local pork, spices and fresh basil, scrambled farm egg, sharp cheddar cheese on a croissant ($8.50). We ordered both sides, hash brown, potato au-gratin with cheddar and chives ($3.99) and cheese grits, 'Beaver Dam Creek' local stone-ground grits with parmesan cheese and roasted tomato, garnished with sweet local basil ($4.99). And if that wasn't enough, we got the cinnamon and sugar crepe, Hatcher Dairy butter, cinnamon sugar, maple syrup ($4.50). You can tell they really work fast in that truck, it didn't take but ten minutes maybe for all the food to come out. I've always thought that most food trucks usually charge more than one would pay in a restaurant. This might be because of the convenience of it, but I think Crepe A Diem's prices are spot on. You get QUALITY food and it's not a little portion either. This garden sausage sandwich was a monster. I really loved the pork sausage inside, it was seasoned well and paired well with the cheese. Same goes for the Louisiana crepe. The sausage in that was so flavorful. I'm not a huge fan of red peppers or onions but loved this. The sides were great as well. This hash brown is probably one of the best I've ever had. I like this thing better than most places french fries. And the grits, can you say 'cheese'!? I've never really liked grits but this these didn't taste like your average grits. Lastly the cinnamon sugar crepe was a nice way to cleanse the palate after a hearty breakfast from Crepe A Diem. We will be back.

text: My wife and I live in Arkansas, but still have Saints' season tickets, so we visit New Orleans pretty often. This past weekend, we brought a friend with us. We drove down on Friday and arrived about 6pm. After dinner at the Palace Cafe (subject of another review) we ended up at Razzoo's on Bourbon St. Good music, drinks, fun. They have a stage with live entertainment, several bars, an outdoor patio, plenty of bathrooms, and even when the place is crowded, you don't feel jammed in. This recent trip turned out to be very special, as you will understand if you read the rest of my review. Not long after we arrived, a friend in our party got her wallet picked out of her purse. (It was unzipped.) She noticed it immediately after, and we notified one of the security guys at the door. Within seconds, there were multiple employees around, including the manager on duty, asking questions. They went and checked the security video, and got perfect images of the two thieves. Several of the security guys spread into the French Quarter while one of them took a copy of the video to the local police precinct two blocks away. My wife and I accompanied our friend to the police station to file a police report, but not really expecting that much would result from it. Were we wrong. Within two hours of the theft, the two culprits were arrested by a Louisiana state trooper. One of Razzoo's security guys was combing the Quarter, came across the perps with another mark, and grabbed a trooper who was assigned to that street. The two were arrested without a problem. A search turned up nothing but a couple of hundred dollars in cash. The manager on duty was named Reuben, and he told us that Razzoo's had recently put in a new security camera system. After the state trooper showed us his copy of the video, it was obvious that the investment by the club was worth the money. The clarity of the picture was perfect and it identified the thieves without question. Turned out that one of the arrested pickpockets had just been paroled from prison the day before after serving 25 years of a 40-year sentence for murder. (!) So much for that early release. We will go to Razzoo's more often after this experience. Part 2 - The next morning, our friend got a call from a woman from Florida who had found her personal effects in an alley where the thieves discarded them after the crime. She had googled our friend's name, found her on LinkedIn, saw her resume online that included the phone number and called. (The wonders of modern technology.) We met with the woman and her husband later that day, and our friend got her driver's license, credit cards, personal papers, etc all returned to her. (I have to admit that if I hadn't seen all this with my own eyes, I never would have believed that this kind of outcome was possible.) Thank you, Razzoo's for reminding us that there are more good people in our society than bad. Note: The club is undergoing renovations on their patio area this week and announced that they would be closed for a few days while this work is going on. If you walk by and they're open, go.

The owner is a New York native, moved to Philly and opened this restaurant 3 years ago. All of the staff were really truly very nice and professional. We ordered 4 small plates and shared 1 dessert. The kitchen gave us 2 complimentary appetizers (potato soup with parsley oil, tuna tartare with crushed rice crackers), which were really nice. I have to mention that the sourdough toast they sell for only $1 is very good as well. Maryland Crab on toast: the owner Ms. Vernick recommended it. Lump crab meat spread generously on toasts. Light and delicious. The special pasta of the day: Tagliatelle tossed in light sauce with sausage and red currants. The combination of savory sausage and sweet currants was amazing. My boyfriend loves more tender pasta, and it was cooked just right for him. Arctic Char, Crispy Skin & Dill: The fish was carefully prepared. Just fish, non-greasy crispy skin and bits of dill, but it leaves a very fresh feeling in your mouth. Grilled Heart of Romaine, Figs, Aged Cheddar: This might have been the best grilled romaine I have ever had, just as when I was more than ready to forget this dish for good. The romaine is warm on the outside, very juicy and crisp inside. Just a little too salty on the soft leaves, but not bad enough for me to take one star off. The addition of figs stuffed in the romaine is unforgettably tasty. The Date Cake: A nice portion for two people to share. Not too sweet yet so satisfying! I only wish I didn't manage to stop myself from getting the last bite... Also, as we were sitting by the kitchen, I was watching the kitchen staff and food runners closely. They were very serious about making food - the chef reads a timer for every dish, and the food runners were always waiting at the counter. The guy at the back was spending 2 minutes on cleaning one single glass, literally. We never heard chitchat during the course of our dinner. These are serious food lovers/makers, which explains why Vernick has received many compliments on Yelp. Can't wait to come back!

text: Background: I grew up in CA eating tacos and burritos from local taquerias from SD to SF until a few years ago. I've eaten tacos in the Southwest and the Northeast so I've taken certain things in stride. These are "approximately" CA tacos. They are double-tortilla (because they are too big) and have a lot of guero extras on them that are unnecessary, and asking for cilantro and onion only results in a sprinkling of both rather than an acceptable portion. The guacamole has no pico in it, and thus little flavor. The pastor isn't sweet and savory and is missing the hot piña slice (common in Florida for some reason). The chorizo is chunky and not smooth. Ricos/street tacos are called "TJ tacos". You can't mix and match these tacos which makes no sense. The price is too high for what you get ($2+ for a fountain drink). They should get 3 stars for these obvious heretical transgressions. That said, the pico is baller; the hot sauce is baller, the carnitas are baller, the asada is baller. The tacos are too big but they are borderline baller. The Godzilla burrito will slay a donkey. And, most importantly, there just aren't any places doing it better unless you sit down. So I am begrudgingly giving it a 4-stars. I've eaten here 4 times in 3 weeks. The hot sauce is what's doing it for me, it's what I want from my taco place.

On the not so bright side...goodness...where do I begin? I'll start out by saying it was a light traffic day...maybe 4-5 other tables were occupied during our stay. The owner of the restaurant was casually sitting at a corner table, disengaged and disinterested in what was going in the restaurant. After we ordered our food, it took over 30 minutes before we received anything (besides chips). With such light traffic, I can't find any excuse as to the long wait. The lengthy delay became evident when we noticed our beans & rice, once delivered, were completely cold. Not lukewarm, but chilled and bland...as if they had been sitting out on the counter for a good, long while. On top of that, three of the four orders were incorrect in some capacity. For instance, my mother-in-law ordered corn tortillas with her meal, but was given flour tortillas instead. When she asked for corn tortillas a second time, it took another 20 minutes before they were brought out. Needless to say, she wasn't very happy...and felt completely devalued as a customer. For me, personally, I knew something was off when I ordered a diet coke with lime...and it came out a diet coke with lemon (granted, this by itself is a small deal). But the cold beans and rice was a first for me...and I've eaten out hundreds of times at mexican restaurants in the Nashville area the past 6-7 years. On top of this, there was no offer of a partial refund on any part of our order to account for the multiple mishaps. So, that was additional salt on the wound. Overall, the taste was medicore...definitely not anything special to justify the poor service. The prices are fair, but still...I have no clue why the ratings are so high with this place. Now, I assume we simply caught them on a bad day; however, it doesn't change the fact our experience was highly disappointing...and judging by what I'm hearing, the quality of service and management has dropped fast in 2015. So hopefully this establishment can get its act together quickly. As for me, I don't plan on coming back...but hopefully, things change for others who dine there.

text: WOW! That is all I can say. I have to say that NONE of them even compare to this. Winter Wonderland has over 1 million lights and many of them create some pretty great illusions. I found out about it online. It is $10 per car ($20 per limo, $40 per commercial van, and $90 per tour bus). It is WELL worth the money. There was every light display possible at this place.....from all of the reindeer (see if you can find all 9) to Frosty to Santa to every single Christmas light display you could think of. So many of them are interactive and they are just so incredibly colorful. A description wouldn't do it justice. The display opened tonight and runs through January 2. They also have carriage rides during that time as well, which range from $55 to $120. I think you need reservations for these. Some helpful hints: 1. Get someone else to drive! I drove through and couldn't enjoy it nearly as much because I was convinced I was going to rear-end the car in front of me. 2. Enter south bound from McKnight Road. I think this is the only entrance. 3. You can only drive or take a carriage through the display. They previously sold tickets for you to be able to walk through, but that was only November 20-22 (and they sold out!). 4. Bring cash or check to pay at the end. They don't take credit cards. 5. Tune your radio to 90.1 (I believe). There is a sign early during the display that lists the radio station. To think Popeye's was the gold standard of fast food chicken at one time. Seems like the entire fast food industry is in a transitional period. text: Sadly, I am removing my previous, very positive review of El Sarape and replacing it with this one, which is the opposite: completely negative. And yet the food is still great, the wait staff still welcoming and highly competent. So what changed my opinion? One awful experience. And that is the lesson I'm trying to convey: One bad experience can outweigh many good ones. The tale begins with a Groupon we had not been able to use, and which was expiring that day. We called, made a reservation, telling them we had a Groupon that we had just remembered we had. The only table open was just barely doable for us, time-wise, if we rushed, so we left immediately. When we arrived, we once again told them we had a Groupon. When we ordered, we repeated that we had a Groupon, since restaurants always want to be told them about it in advance of ordering. The meal was good. We had bought the Groupon intending to use it with friends (the reason we did not use the Groupon earlier or invite friends to join us comes later in this review), so we ordered more food than we needed in order to use its value. We gave the Groupon to the waitress; after a few minutes she returned and told us they couldn't take it because it was Saturday night and it was only valid from Sunday through Thursday. So there we were, faced with a very large check we had not expected. And this is exactly the situation that every restaurant should try to avoid. No one likes surprises when it comes to money. Noticing the manager, I got up and told her our problem and asked why no one had told us--considering that they had three opportunities to do so--that our Groupon was not valid. She told me there are all sorts of Groupon offers and that "this happens all the time." I noted that the very fact that it "happens all the time" should motivate her to have her staff ask to see the Groupon before people order their food. I mentioned that no one likes to be surprised about money. Most regrettably, the manager actually laughed out loud at my suggestion. I went and sat down, having just been humiliated in front of many people. It got worse--she watched me sit down, made eye contact, and once again snickered, no doubt pleased that she had forced this nasty woman who was obviously trying to pull a fast one to pay her a lot of money. The laughing at me part motivated my husband to go speak to the manager. I should here mention that the reason we had not used the Groupon previously was that he'd had a heart attack. This was the first time since leaving the hospital we had gone out; we were trying to have a quiet dinner to celebrate the fact that he was alive. Yes, it was on us to have checked the Groupon more closely. But sometimes the reasons people do dumb things is not that they are stupid or dishonest. Sometimes they have a lot of more important things on their minds. The hospitality business is about knowing that, not about shaming people, laughing at them or insulting them. Yet not at El Sarape! Oh my no! The manager was just as rude to my husband as she'd been to me. She asked him what he wanted her to do. He told her he wanted her to honor the Groupon. She told him not to tell her how to run her business. Seriously, those are her exact words, after specifically asking him what he wanted her to do! I have never experienced quite that level of arrogance in a restaurant. The manager did grudgingly give us a gift card, but didn't tell us how much it's worth. Frankly, I expect it has $5.00 on it, but even if it was $5,000.00 we will not be returning to any of the Sarape restaurants (El Sarape and the two Los Sarapes, all owned by the same people). Ever.

text: If, one day, you wake up in the morning and think to yourself: 'I would like to be robbed today. Just completely, absolutely, ripped off.' .. Then Runway Fashion Exchange is THE place for you.
