You take in your bags of nice, clean, brand name clothes that cost you countless HUNDREDS of dollars (i.e. North Face, Nike, Under Armour, Patagonia, Rock Revival) and let the employees pick through them with looks on their faces as if you just brought in a bag full of your grandmother's moth ridden cruise-wear. Then, after that horrible chore is all done, you'll be called back up to the front where they have a steel bin that they've thrown the things they deemed acceptable in to, and the unwanted clothing is put back into your bags for you to pack off. This, though. This here is my favorite part. It's the part when they stop, look you in the eye, and blatantly offer you PENNIES on the dollar for your things - yet, somehow, make it seem as if it's not a bad thing. Not a bad thing at all. Instead, it's made to seem as if they're doing you a gigantic favor by taking these items off of your hands, and that they'll hardly profit at all. Apparently quadrupling their money isn't as great of a profit as they'd like. Bummer for them. Now for some reason - maybe it was the full blown shock that had set in, that possibly hindered my decision making abilities - I actually accepted their offer, took my measly $20.10, and left. Looking back, I wish nothing more than that I would've stood up for myself, taken those items, and sold them myself on Craigslist for easily three times more. In closing, I will never be returning to this horrible place. Not to buy, not to sell. I only hope you'll learn from my mistake, and stay away before you too, get screwed over. Maybe if enough people stay away, this Runway will take their stolen profits, and move on.

text: My best friend and I stumbled upon this place accidentally. Kind of. Thinking it was a different restaurant that we had been to before, I asked her to meet me here for happy hour last week. It turned out that the reason the place sounded familiar was not because we'd been here before, but because I'd had it bookmarked for years and had never made it down. Oops! Happy accident. Azie was difficult for me to find. It's in a shopping center of sorts, in that there are other businesses in a cluster of small buildings close to one another. There is a sign right off the road for Azie, so you know that you're in the right area, but it still took me five minutes driving around all the buildings to find the right one. Just so you know, it's behind the back left building, up an incline a bit. The restaurant was definitely nicer than I was expecting. It has a very classy feel to it, very quiet and calming as well. So we were super surprised at how awesome the happy hour was! From 5-7, they had several $5 glasses of wine (not just the one or two whites and reds that some places do), most beers on special, and their version of $5 you-call-its. They had one vodka, rum, gin, tequila, scotch and bourbon on special, and you could order any kind of drink with that alcohol for $5. $5 martinis, yes please!! The happy hour food menu was super large as well. The food wasn't priced as low as the drinks, but I noticed the regular menu was priced high as well. So the HH food specials were still a great deal based off of their regular menu. There were around a dozen sushi rolls you could get at a discount. We tried the spicy tuna ($5 or $6), spicy scallop ($8), and shrimp tempura rolls($5). All were delicious. Then we tried the tuna pizza, crab and cream cheese spring rolls ($4), and mussels ($6) in a thai curry sauce. We ordered this smorgasboard for you, Yelpers, not just for our stomachs. Possibly. The tuna pizza was a misnomer, because they turned out to be delicious tuna nachos. Raw tuna on top of tortilla chips topped with sriracha and lots of roe. The mussels had good flavor and we loved the Thai curry sauce, but the mussels were small. Great for happy hour sharing, but I would hope that the portion on the dinner menu is a little larger. I already have plans to go for HH next week, and will update review when I go back for a real meal. Definitely two thumbs up so far though!

text: Golden Nugget is a Godsend! I flew to Ethiopia to surprise my (now) Fianceé last November. FATEEMA EVANS was my salesperson and her service was exemplary! Needless to say, Golden Nugget was my first stop in engagement ring shopping across the world and indubitably my last. I seriously could not ask for a better experience if I had a thousand more lifetimes and ten thousand more girlfriends to propose to. Fateema took my situation personally and was professional during my entire transaction -- from the very beginning when I was *just browsing* to the transition of making the ring my own. The store was decorated with the most gorgeous stones I have ever seen and awesome quality. Fateema handled things so seamlessly and I've honestly gained a new friend in her -- not just a salesperson. There was never a time when Fateema made me feel less than comfortable. My girlfriend had never been to America yet and considering I was flying to Africa to get engaged, I needed help and an honest shoulder to lean on. Fateema spent the time with me -- viewing dozens of photos of my girlfriend to analyze how the ring would look on her finger, analyzing finger sizes in the photos and so forth. Unlike most men who's girlfriend goes to the store with them and picks their OWN ring out, and the man proposes two months later as she acts surprised, I didn't have that luxury. I had to get it right on the first time. Fateema was an angel. Also, the rest of the staff was terrific, including a few of the other salespeople who's service was beautiful, and the owner. I flew to Africa months later with my ruby, proposed to my Fianceé, and there was a video made from the proposal that made national news in Ethiopia. Fateema was very involved and sent me a heartfelt email telling me that she was praying for me and rooting for us. As it turned out, my Fianceé's fingers looked a little chunkier on photo than they were in real life. The ring was a tad too big for my damsel, so the owner suggested that I bring it back to get it serviced to protect myself and the micro pave diamonds. I followed his instructions and Fateema resized and cleaned it for free -- with a very quick turnaround of 1 day. My fianceé was ELATED at the ring I selected for her and it meant everything to see her face when I proposed. I will remember this forever. When it comes to Golden Nugget, understand me when I tell you that I couldn't have made a better choice, period. I've traveled the world but have never received service quite like this. My father has purchased all of his jewelry at Golden Nugget for over a decade and I now understand why. As long as they're in business, my unborn grandsons will be buying their engagement rings here. Also, I have sent many friends their way and will continue to do so. I am the author of "The Book of G.A.M.E." and I may even give them a plug on my next book. Fateema and Golden Nugget has definitely found a friend in me!

text: Writing a bad review is tough as you don't want to come off as jilted or overly negative but in our case we felt, that after working with PtoP on resolution, we needed to share our experience with everyone we can. We used PtoP based on the recommendation of our agent. They liked that it was a "one stop shop" for all the inspections rather than having to schedule each one separately and also liked that the report is generated on site rather than having to wait. We felt the price of the inspection was a little high but did appreciate the convenience and turn around time so went forward with them. On the day of inspection we met the inspector and another guy that I believe was in training. At the same time we had the other inspectors showing up as well. Overall, it was a typical inspection where they'd call out anything specific they wanted us to review. Overall they noted nothing major other than some water coming in around the existing roof penetrations. There were a handful of other cosmetic/best practice recommendations. The report had a section at the front for the items that needed addressed and we reviewed those that morning after they were done. Overall, it was a smooth transaction and inspection (other than a snafu with the sewer inspection but that wasn't PtoP's issue). The guys were very friendly and it was a nice morning process. After moving in though we started finding things they didn't: - The biggest item of concern is we found that significant wood rot was found on a sun-room that we'll either have to totally rip off or invest significantly to repair. Detailed below. - We noticed that the showers weren't inspected. One drain still had a layer of dirt/dust so we know they didn't run the shower to test it otherwise it'd have been rinsed. The drain in the master bath filled with water the first time we took a shower as it was nearly plugged so clearly they didn't test that either otherwise we'd expect the report to suggest service on the drain. - The exhaust fans in the same two bathrooms were unplugged in the ceiling. Not a big deal but clearly not tested so if they didn't work we'd have not caught it before the purchase. - The more detailed report (not reviewed on site) said the attic space wasn't inspected b/c it would be dangerous. The attic is fully lit and has plywood from wall to wall so you can walk through it. - We have a full 4" or bigger hole on the side of the house from an unused stove vent. Only thing on the report was a small note about filling hole penetrations around wires. I spoke with the owner of the PtoP franchise and he was very very good to work with. I stress that - very professional and courteous. He asked that i let the previous inspector come back out to document the miss. Several weeks later I met him and he reviewed the rotted area (as that was the primary concern). Note we've since found another rotted section but at the time only one was being discussed. Again the inspector was nice but his position was that if the sellers were hiding it they can't be expected to find it. I called out the other missed items that were basic drawing attention to the lack of detail and focus on our inspection. I also called out that I, a casual home owner and not a professional inspector, found the rotted section just by happenstance and noted the un-hidden water damage signs around the problem. That generally ended the conversation and it was back to the franchise owner for next steps. End result was a full refund of the inspection. But, and this is what bothers me, the criteria for a refund was that I waive ALL liability for future claims due to the missed inspection items. Repair of the single section is north of $5k without accounting for window replacement. Now we're looking at the other section as well that's rotted out on a different wall. So the Sunroom as a whole is facing $10k in repairs. Easily something that could have been negotiated out during the home purchase. I don't expect PtoP to be accountable for the loss of value and cost of full repair, but I do think it's bad business for them to hold a refund hostage pending a release of liability. It really looks like they too are worried they missed other major items on our house. Very long story short - They don't stand behind their inspection clearly by asking that we release them of liability to refund the purchase price.

text: My kids have been in daycare since they were 6 weeks old. I enrolled both of my kids (now 1 and 3) at Kids R Kids because the daycare they were going to had closed. I never found the staff at Kids R Kids to be very friendly, or nurturing towards my kids. Also, the teachers were unable to tell my children 'No'. I am all for 'redirection' learning, but if my child is drawing on walls, I feel that they need to be told that is isn't okay to do that, and tell them 'No'. My kids only went to Kids R Kids for 4 months, during these 4 months my kids became pretty wild. They stopped listening, everything was a fight, we were late everyday - and yes I know, they are 1 and 3, but it was absolute complete chaos! It was outside of the norm of chaos. Kid R Kids has the Watch me Grow system, so I was able to watch my child during the day. Every day they have their learning activities and all the children will sit in a group on the carpet, instead of my child participating I would see my child be redirected to the classroom table practically every day, because they wouldn't just tell her to stop acting up, sit down and listen. Instead they would redirect her to the classroom table with a book (of course she is unable to read by herself because she is 3). So she wasn't able to participate in the learning activities. As we are working parents, this daycare center just wasn't working for us. So I pulled them out and moved them to another daycare center. I have waited a of couple months to write this review, but in the last two months my kids are doing so much better, they have respect for others again, they are listening, we are back to the normal chaos, and we are never late anymore. After the first 3 weeks my 3 year old was at their new daycare, she even said to me 'Mommy they don't sit me down to read books by myself anymore' - SERIOUSLY I could not even believe that she said that to me! It breaks my heart the way they are doing business at this daycare center. Kids R Kids is a place where they are just running a business, I don't feel that they actually give individual nurturing attention to the kids that are there. A few additional things that I didn't like... 1. About 90% of the time I walked in to pick up my kids the reception people would never make eye contact. 2. They always forgot I had two kids, and they could never remember who my kids were when I asked them questions. I'm sorry, when I am paying you $400 a week, I feel that you should at least know who my kids are. 3. They feed the kids a lot of junk food in the afternoon. I buy candy and cookies, but every day they would have cookies, brownies, pop tarts... just not the healthiest place. 4. It also didn't seem the teachers in my kids classrooms could think for themselves, the front staff seemed to make all the calls, which I did not like because they weren't the ones actually in the classroom every day with my child. An example, one day I dropped my 3 year old off, she said she didn't feel good. She didn't have a fever and didn't have any symptoms. I asked her teacher to call me if she didn't eat her morning snack or her lunch, and I would come pick her up before nap time. Well when the time came for her lunch and they didn't call me I felt everything was just fine. Well then front desk called me at 3pm and let me know she hadn't eaten all day. It took them 3 hours to call me. I was so infuriated! Complete lack of communication because the teacher was unable to call me herself, and 5. My kids got Hand, Foot and Mouth... I know this can go through all daycares, but... it is weird that I was warned about it from a friend before my kids attended Kids R Kids. I do not recommend this daycare to anyone. I went and checked out a pre-school for my 3 year old and they were more personable within the 20 minutes I was there taking a tour than Kids R Kids ever was in the 4 months my kids attended. In 4 months we just had way many problems.

text: Oh Pho, how I love thee. That being said, I've had my share of this Vietnamese bowl of deliciousness around Philly and up and down the East Coast. Unfortunately, my hometown city always came up a bit short. There are great Vietnamese restaurants here, but I've never been wowed by their pho. Enter Saigon Cuisine. Tucked on the corner of 40th Street where University City and West Philly meet is this small gem. Hell, it's directly next to an equally small Indian and Thai restaurant. So at quick glance you may lose it in the shuffle. But it's there, and it's worth the look. The outside, I'll admit, may throw you. The sign is a bit dingy, there's an empty lot half a block down, can't see inside to even see of the place is open. But. Once you step in all if your fears are put away Inside is bright with bamboo floor (I think) with red booths and tables, modern pop music playing in the background and a single TV on mute with what looks to be a Vietnamese news station. Oh, and the smell. You'd live in a dumpster if it smelled like this restaurant. I got here on a Monday at Noon with a friend and we were seated promptly. Plenty of booths and had an ok crowd. Maybe about 1/3 full. Our waitress immediately took got us water and handed menus. The menu here is small but gets the point across. I ordered the brisket pho (large) and steamed pork dumplings. While my friend ordered beef eye pho and summer rolls. The food (minus my dumplings) were out in no time. Which tells me they have this stuff at the ready. Good move, ownership. The summer rolls we're bulky, full of greens and shrimp and came with a sweet peanut sauce for dipping. My dumplings came out fresh, hot, and with a little sear on them from the grill. Also with a dipping sauce. And once they were cooled I couldn't keep them out of my mouth. So sad when I had gone through my serving of 5. Now the pho. Our waitress started by bringing out a plate of bean sprouts, jalapeños, sliced limes and a bottle of soy sauce. I was super excited when I saw that huge bowl coming my way. I could smell the spices before our waitress even put them down. The bowl was pretty big. Definitely a large bowl if there ever was one. The meat was tender in sliced pieces making them flavorful and easy to eat, the noodles were cooked to perfection. The broth at the end was so good I had to forego the spoon and drink it from the bowl. So, needless to say I am a fan if this small slice of pho heaven. The only reason it's 4/5 stars is the wait staff. I get it was a slow lunch rush and there weren't many people in but to see the entire staff with their noses buried in their phones within view of the customers was a bit off putting. I don't wanna bash too hard. Because when it was game time our waitress came ready to play. We didn't wait too long for food or refills or anything. I guess it just seemed unprofessional to see them all in the phone. But other than that, they were great. I'll definitely be dining here again when I need a pho fix.

text: Great restaurant, fun vibe and creative thoughtful menu. I have been here a few times now and after reading several of the reviews, especially from those who have only been there once, I am amazed at how critical people can be. The atmosphere is a bit on the loud side, but what do you expect when your in a fun open setting. That makes it all the more interesting. If I wanted quiet, I would have stayed home. The booths are my favorite, big and comfortable with enough space for a large party and still with elbow room to eat. Our booth was an awesome spot to do the south tampa people watch, and what a scene it is! Loved that I could meld into the beautiful woodwork and enjoy. Our dinner was exceptionally enjoyable from the time the host greeted us to when our waiter wished a safe ride home. Stating with the wines by the glass, smart to have Italian choices. I tend to be a creature of habit so to not sway too far off my normal Sonoma Chardonnay they offered me a delicious Il Borro white. Smooth and refreshing, loved it. Also the wine glasses themselves have a clever design that allows each glass to breath. I thought there was a crack in the glass but when the owner stopped by to say hello, he explained how they work and swirled my husbands red. The attention to detail is truly amazing and I haven't even gotten to the food. We had the luxury of asking the owner bit more about the menu and he went on to share with us how each morning the bread is kneaded and baked in the wood oven, and that each of the cavatelli pastas are hand rolled. Reminded me of my great Italian aunts' pasta dishes. I had to order both! And I wasn't disappointed, it brought me back. The pasta was tender and flavorful and the sauce was fresh and simple. Not overbearing and heavy. The perfect balance and the right amount. So tired of the large oversized portions. The table also ordered the muscles with more of the scrumptious bread. While I am not a muscles person, I could have devoured the sauce by myself. Along with the smokey flavor of the bread dipped in the sauce, the combination was heaven. Another guest with us had the Kale Salad and the meatballs. Wow another great combo choice. Love the Kale in the tempura batter, crispy, tangy and spectacular. And the meatballs, something I have been known to make mean one myself, were presented by themselves with no sauce. Very daring since a meatball without sauce better be pretty darn good. Again they were flavorful, and spices used were the right amount to complement the meat. Our daughter ordered the margherita pizza and loved the flavor of the crust but would have liked a bit more cheese. (and what kid wouldn't like more). Anyway it was definitely reminiscent of the pizzas we had in Italy, so again kudos to the authenticity of everything Ava's is doing. Yes I'm a fan! See you at Ava's soon.

text: Why is Walmart still in business?! I go to this particular Walmart every once in a while, because I usually hate Walmart but found this one to be not as bad as the others. I was wrong. It sure didn't take long for this place to become as deplorable as every other Walmart location. I only went this time because I needed a prescription filled that my insurance doesn't cover. A friend told me that I could save money by buying it at Walmart (and I DID save $25.00). My doctor called the prescription in at 1:00, (afternoon) and I figured if I went at 8:30 p.m., I could run in and pick it up really quickly without having to wait. Wishful thinking!!!!!! There was a pharmacist and 2 male employees working... or should I say NOT working. The pharmacist was helping a couple in front of me. I waited in line for 15 minutes (of which NO ONE even glanced in my direction), before I finally called out to one of the lazy employees in the back,"Are you guys open or what?" One of them reluctantly came to help me. He asked for my name about 5 times. I spelled it for him SIX times. He finally tells me I'm not in the computer. The pharmacist overhears and then comes over. He tells me,"Oh, your prescription must have been on one of the voicemail messages that were called in. We're backed up, and I have about 10 of them I haven't gotten to." Mind you, there are about 6 customers behind me in line. He tells me it will only be a few minutes. I said,"Okay," and went to sit down and play a game on my phone. After about 5 minutes, I look up, and see the pharmacist is waiting on customers. He never went to the back to work on my prescription. I sat and waited patiently, trying not to think of the impending snowstorm and my 30 minute drive home. After about 20 minutes, I couldn't take it any more. I stood up and called to one of the guys in the back,"So.... will I get my prescription filled tonight, or what?" They looked at each other and laughed, and one made a joke to the other in Spanish. The same guy that helped me earlier asked for my name again (and I spelled it for him again about 3 times), and he told me once again it will be ready in a few minutes. I looked around at all the other customers around me, and only one lady seemed to be bothered by how long it's taking. We started talking, and I found out this was her first time getting a prescription filled there, too. Apparently, the other people were Walmart pharmacy regulars and were accustomed to this substandard treatment. Knowing I had lots of time to spare, I walked over to the customer service desk to see if there was a manager I could complain to. The guy at the desk told me there was a supervisor working at register 4, and that he could could page the manager of the store for me. I thanked him and walked over to register 4. There were about 15 miserable people in line... I was not about to become the 16th!!! That was just too many for me to get in line to make my complaint! I walked back to the pharmacy, feeling defeated. There was absolutely nothing I could do. It was a Friday night, and I would not be able to get in touch with my doctor until Monday for a new prescription. I was STUCK. I had no choice but to sit down and wait. On top of that, my phone battery went dead and I couldn't even play my game. I waited an hour and 26 minutes for my prescription. Considering that they had 7 1/2 hours to have my order ready, it was inexcusable. There were no apologies made WHATSOEVER. I find it appalling that a company can show its customers so little concern and so much disrespect and still be in business.
label: NEG

text: Ever since Animo relocated from this spot I've been anxious to see what would come next, when I saw a Mediterranean restaurant was moving in I was definitely excited! When I think of this type of cuisine I usually think of falafel, before walking into the restaurant this afternoon for lunch I skimmed the menu posted outside and sad I didn't see any falafel offered. Nevertheless the options sounded fresh, appetizing, and interesting. The staff was very cheerful and friendly, I was the only guest in the restaurant and they told me to sit where ever I pleased. The inside is small, cozy, bright, and very clean. There are about 10 tables big enough to seat 4, and would accommodate larger parties by being pushed together, reservations would definitely be recommended on a Friday or weekends. My server introduced herself by name and told me Zaffron's "concept": everything is organic and made fresh daily. They also do not use freezers or fryers. This alone is awesome, it made me even more excited. I ordered the hummus (served which fresh bread) and the Zaffron Signature Salad. The hummus came out first, the presentation was beautiful which balsamic drizzle on the plate, garnished with red pepper slices and dill I believe. The bread was served separately wrapped in a cloth napkin and was still warm. The bread was excellent: soft on the inside and crisp and hard on the outside, it paired excellently with the hummus which tasted just as good as it looked: not too garlicky, very fresh, great balance of flavors. I was starting to fill up on this and eating quite fast as I was very hungry, the sever offered more bread but i declined, I wanted to save room for my salad. When the salad came out I was again impressed with the presentation: a medium sized mound of greens (romaine, arugula, kale, frisee, etc) in a olive oil citrus vinaigrette, feta cheese, tomato, avocado and olives, and more balsamic drizzle. Again very fresh and delicious. The meal was paced appropriately I did not feel rushed, and the server was attentive. I was on my hour lunch break and at the end mentioned I was ready for my check, I would recommend telling you're server at the beginning if you are in a rush, but i was able to enjoy my meal in about an hour at a comfortable pace. There were two more guests who arrived after me, a couple who came in for lunch. The chef/owner made an appearance and introduced himself to the couple I overheard him saying he was from Italy and they were chatting about the food and the restaurant, he also stopped at my table and talked to me as well and was telling me how the hummus is made fresh everyday. I also mentioned to the host that i was surprised that falafel was not on the menu, she said that falafel was Greek and has to be made very well and carefully. I still think they should serve falafel, even only if its served as a Special. Zaffron describes themselves as a Mediterranean so falafel will definitely qualify! I gave them a 4 out of 5 stars however because I think the interior decor was lacking, although everything inside was new and new paint on the walls and very clean, i think the inside was a bit boring the pictures all looked very similar, the music when i first walked in sounded appropriate and had a good vibe but then it switched to a song that i would describe as "elevator music". I was thinking of a more trendy and hip interior for Mediterranean cuisine. I cannot wait however for the weather to warm up to sit outside.The restaurant is still very new and I applaud them on their fresh and yummy cuisine, attentive staff and owner. I will definitely be returning again.
label: POS

text: Everything positive that's been said about the museum to me has been true. "Living museum" comes to mind because this great space doesn't feel static or silent. It was crowded the day we visited and it doesn't feel like the trails are swarming with people or you have to shove people away from shirts in the gift shop. It helps that the grounds are huge. Bring a water bottle. Bring a hat. Kudos to those brave souls who visit in the summer. The gift shop rocks, by the way. (Literally, too! Lots of rocks.) I bought a pair of festively colored javelina socks for a friend and exposed some out-of-towners to prickly pear. Zoo seems more appropriate but it isn't adequate. The botanical garden features are peaceful and informative. The butterfly area smells heavenly. The aquarium was the weak point of our visit, but the aquaria where the beavers and otter are were a favorite. There's above ground and below ground and underwater. There's enclosed, like hummingbirds, and open, like tortoises. The whole museum feels built into the desert rather than built on the desert and you'll spy mountains all along. The drive up is beautiful - there's a trailhead and look-out point along the way that was a prime photo op for the staggering cliffs and prickled landscape. I'm mad it took me so long to make it here but I know now this will be the location I take visitors first.

text: This is my best, objective, opinion of Freight Center based upon my experience and subsequent disagreements with this company over the last 12 months. I had priced the shipping of two kayaks from several carriers and brokers and Freight Center was the lowest price. The rep was extremely helpful, though, in hindsight, he did mention that the a customer he recently worked with had some trouble with overcharges since his items didn't exactly correspond (weight and/or dimensions) to what was apparently provided to this rep. Well, I certainly wish I had listened to that voice in my head warning me that this is an odd place to begin a conversation around a shipping transaction. I gave the exact, dimensions and weight of my kayaks. We talked endlessly about their being bubble-wrapped and not boxed. He explained (very helpfully) about there being no insurance options available from carriers and even recommended a place with whom I could speak (including my own insurance company). Fine, I'll gamble with no insurance as the merchant I purchased the kayaks from assured me they would be fine. After following their strict instructions for labeling, etc. it took an extra few days for the pickup to arrive after many assurances that someone was sent or was on their way. The kayaks were eventually picked up and arrived perfectly at my local shipper. I strapped them to my SUV's roof and drove happily along... ...until shortly after I got home I began getting messages from Freight Center's automated Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system alerting me to the fact that my credit card has been charged $200 because my kayaks weighed 300 pounds over what I reported (more on that later) triggering a new class for my shipment. I tried several times to get a human to speak with and finally did when I threatened to challenge the charges with my credit card company. I was informed that Freight Center was challenging the disputed charge on my behalf and it could take 120 business days to resolve and further, I cannot be part of the process. Great, I'm $200 out and at the mercy of the terms and conditions I signed with Freight Center and must wait 5-6 months. ...5-6 months later and they sided against me. I worked with my credit card company for the next 3 months and two rounds of escalation and my credit card company agreed with me. But that is not the end is it? No. From there I was sent an official notice that their Accounts Payable department would sue me for the money. It is now literally, 12 months later. I was only too happy to hear from them as ALL I EVER WANTED TO DO WAS MAKE MY CASE TO A HUMAN AND NEGOTIATE A SETTLEMENT. I had offered via their CRM system to meet them in the middle and pay $100 (under protest) and heard no response. I made this same offer twice when they threatened to sue and neither time was contacted. I ended up making a deal with the person from accounts payable just to make this year-long horror show go away. BOTTOM LINE: If you deal with Freight Center you will indemnify them for any issues between what you ship and who ships it (standard practice in the industry of course). In my case, I was told that the kayaks were unboxed and that is what actually triggered the overages. In fact, I was informed the carrier (not to be confused with the broker Freight Center) labeled the overages as 300 lbs overweight so the charge would be $200 and not more if actually based on an unboxed shipment. The point is, I had no way to defend myself or choose what class my shipment was. I only know I have the rep accurate information and we had many, many discussions about these items being unboxed and despite that when things went expensively wrong, I had no voice and their terms and conditions bound me to silence. Freight Center, you preach Customer Service at every opportunity. I just don't see it and certainly didn't feel it. Your automated system is cold and rigid and it seems you hide behind it. In my case, a conversation would have saved us both money as you paid for two charge backs from my credit card company. I hope this review is helpful. If you use this or another shipping broker ask them what can go wrong, what will happen if things do go wrong and what can be done upfront to assure nothing does. Good luck.

We started off with Bruschetta as our opener, which was an absolute delight. There were so many flavors combined together that just made it PERFECT, in my opinion. It is definitely an opener that I would suggest to all first time diners. Also, it is only $6 during happy hour, so you're getting a deal for what you get. As for our entrees, I would have to say they were "so-so", especially for the price you're paying. The presentation was great, as well as the proportions, but I feel they were lacking seasoning for they were a little on the bland side. My husband ordered the pan-seared duck, which was good, but not great. In my opinion, it could have been more flavorful. As for my entree, I ordered the vegan sweet potato gnocchi (I also added chicken & parmesan to it, since I'm not vegan). This dish also came with a good proportion, but was also on the bland side. For our dessert, we ordered the triple chocolate cake, and OMG this is to DIE for! We didn't want to get too stuffed, so we didn't make it an "a la mode" (which I slightly regret now), but it was delicious as is. It is an absolute MUST TRY. Overall, if I could, I would rate this review with 3.5 stars, just because I feel as if they still need time to tweak the menu/recipes a slight bit more and also straighten up their staff slightly (we couldn't even find our waitress a few times and sat with empty drinks). They are a new restaurant, so I definitely would not hold it against them for now. I would still recommend this spot to everyone to try. I think it would be the best place to swing by during lunch to stop for a couple drinks and snack on openers for sure. My companion loves oysters so I gave him mine (mind you, I did tell the hostess that my companion eats fish). This part of our meal we enjoyed and I enjoyed my spinach salad :-) Before the main courses, we had a nice strawberry sorbetto. As I mentioned above, our mains were the duck breast with a mushroom risotto (the rice was well cooked, however, bland in taste) whereas my companion had the "ravioli" (a bit saltier than he expected). We enjoyed out mains fine, however, given the expectations based on the adjectives given to the food prepared here, I am willing to say the food was good, but not "phenomenal" or "amazing" based on others' experiences. Before anyone mentions it, the restaurant had two seatings, one at 6pm and one at 8pm. Staff was not running around and as far as the "busy" factor, it was steady. This was a nice thing, actually since it gave everyone a chance to eat tranquilly without worrying to rush and also the staff to serve without rushing. For mains we ordered the hanger steak au poivre which was extra juicy and tender and came with a side of parmiggiano reggiano fries as well as chicken paillard (paillard basically means that it is a chicken breast beaten into flat halves and sautéed).
